chunks: Saʿīd al-Aʿraj asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

About a man who helps a woman down from the litter and draws her close to himself while he is in ihram, so he عليه السلام said: “There is no harm, unless he does so deliberately, and he has more right to help her down than anyone else.”

key_terms.الْمَحْمِلِ: the litter or riding seat from which the woman is helped down
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: a person in the state of ihram for hajj or ʿumrah
key_terms.يَتَعَمَّدَ: he does it intentionally or deliberately
key_terms.يَضُمُّهَا: he draws her close or holds her to support her

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a muhrim to help a woman down from her mount and hold her while doing so?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning physical contact while in the state of ihram. It indicates that helping a woman dismount is permissible when needed, but not if done deliberately in an improper manner or with intentional desire.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2714 - Saeed al-A'raj asked Abu Abdullah (as) about a man who helps a woman down from her mount and holds her close while in the state of ihram.
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm in it unless he does so intentionally [with inappropriate intent], and he has more right to help her down than others."
